entities.summary:
Étienne de Poncher (1446–1524) was a French prelate and diplomat who played a crucial role in shaping the religious and political landscape of France during the Late Middle Ages. A close advisor to King Louis XI, Poncher became president of the Chambre des Enquêtes in 1498 and continued to serve as councillor at the parlement of Paris until his death in 1524. His diplomatic efforts helped to maintain peace between France and its Catholic neighbors, while also promoting the interests of the French monarchy. Poncher's legacy extends to the development of the French legal system, which he helped to codify during his tenure as president of the Chambre des Enquêtes. His contributions to the field of religious diplomacy have also been widely recognized, with many historians noting his role in mediating disputes between the Catholic Church and the French monarchy. As a key figure in the politics of the Late Middle Ages, Poncher's influence can still be felt today, making him an important figure to study for anyone interested in the history of France and the Catholic Church.

Poncher was born in the late 15th century, although the exact date of his birth is unknown. He studied law and was provided with a prebend at an early age, which allowed him to begin his career as a diplomat and advisor to the French monarchy. Poncher's early success led to his appointment as councillor at the parlement of Paris in 1485, where he quickly established himself as a key figure in the royal court.

Despite his many accomplishments, Poncher's life was not without controversy. He was involved in several high-profile disputes with the Catholic Church, including a notable disagreement with the Archbishop of Reims over the question of papal authority. These conflicts, however, did not seem to have any lasting impact on Poncher's career, which continued to thrive until his death in 1524.
